top_story: Trump’s 23 March threat to destroy Iran’s power infrastructure if Tehran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz sharpened a Gulf security crisis and drew explicit Iranian warnings of wider regional retaliation, reinforcing a baseline of energy insecurity that reaches beyond military signaling. That pressure now intersects with a longer-term economic realignment as the UAE says it will leave OPEC and OPEC+ on 1 May 2026, signaling a strategic hedge that could weaken collective oil coordination at a moment of elevated market and maritime risk. On 14 May, a state-backed Jerusalem Day march turned into anti-Arab mob violence in the Old City, with far-right Israeli nationalists openly calling for attacks on Palestinian communities and deepening the sense that official politics are enabling communal aggression. Together, these developments point to a region where coercive state strategy, fraying multilateral frameworks, and licensed sectarian mobilization are converging to raise both political volatility and civilian vulnerability.
